title: Introduce retention-fenceposts and expirable-materialized-views for per-customer analytics erasure
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Objective: Add a low-cost, auditable mechanism to expire customer-scoped analytics derived artifacts without full-table scans. We will introduce retention-fenceposts (logical cut points) and expirable materialized views (EMVs) that store event pointers + compact expiry tokens rather than full PII payloads. Goal is to reduce deletion latency from days to minutes for targeted erasures and to provide cryptographically verifiable attestations for compliance requests.

Scope: Console backend analytics (event-level aggregated metrics, session traces, usage histograms) ingested by the streaming pipeline (kafka -> flume-lite -> materialize) and the nearline OLAP tables used by dashboards. This work does NOT change raw ingestion retention for raw blob storage; focus is on derived analytics products and the Console telemetry index.

High-level design:
- Retention-fenceposts: create per-customer monotonic fencepost markers (fencepost_id, created_at, expire_at, schema_version) emitted when retention policy changes or on scheduled intervals. Each analytics artifact (EMV row, rollup) references the fencepost_id active when it was materialized. Deleting a customer only requires marking the fencepost expire_at and scheduling compaction to drop rows referencing expired fenceposts.
- Expirable Materialized Views (EMVs): materialized aggregations store compact pointers to event primary keys plus a 256-bit deletion token (HMAC of event_key + fencepost_id). The actual PII payloads are not duplicated in EMVs. EMVs support fast predicate of fencepost_id <= expired_marker.
- Compact compaction worker: background job that scans EMV partitions and rewrites segments excluding expired fencepost rows using index-aware compaction. Designed to be I/O-efficient and rate-limited per-customer to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.
- Attestation and audit log: generate signed attestations when a fencepost compaction completes (fencepost_id, num_rows_removed, time_window, signature). Store attestation in compliance ledger (append-only) for audit.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end deletion request for an average-size customer (<30M events) completes within 30 minutes with no >10% latency impact to other queries.
- Attestations generated and queryable within 1 hour.
- No PII left in EMVs or downstream rollups after compaction (verified by randomized checksum tests).

Implementation plan:
1) Data model changes: add fenceposts table, add fencepost_id column to EMV schemas, migration tooling to backfill current rows with a default fencepost.
2) Ingestion changes: annotate materialize jobs with active fencepost on materialization; for streaming jobs, ensure metadata propagated in headers.
3) Compaction worker: implement in Go as a standalone service with a scheduler that respects region/burst limits. Use existing compaction framework used by data-platform to reuse connectors.
4) Attestation service: leverage existing signing key in KMS; produce attestations and write to compliance S3 prefix and a small metadata table (audit-compact-index).
5) Rollout: feature-flag controlled. Start with opt-in "sandbox-customer" group to validate metrics and resource usage.
6) Backfill: run backfill job to assign fencepost_id for historical EMV data. Backfill will stream changes and throttle.

Operational considerations and monitoring:
- New metrics: compaction throughput (rows/sec), compaction lag, compaction error-rate, attestation-generation-latency.
- Cost controls: per-customer compaction budget, global compaction concurrency limiter.
- Recovery: compaction worker supports resumable checkpoints; retain tombstone manifests for 30 days before physical GC.
- Rollback: if compaction causes regressions, we can pause compaction and replay from pre-compaction snapshot (SST backup).

Testing:
- Unit tests for fencepost assignment and HMAC token generation.
- Integration tests using production-like sample: generate synthetic customers with PII-shaped payloads; validate compaction removes rows and attestations match removed counts.
- Chaos test: kill the compaction worker during compaction to validate resumability and idempotency.

Migration risks and mitigations:
- Risk: backfill IO spike. Mitigate by shard-aware, rate-limited backfill and incremental windows.
- Risk: mismatch between materialization and fencepost assignment for windows crossing policy changes. Mitigate by using epoch-based gating and double-writing a transition fencepost during change window.
- Risk: incorrect attestations. Mitigate by adding independent verifier job that repros counts from a separate sampling pipeline.

Open questions:
- Policy enforcement granularity: per-customer vs per-organization sub-scoping (needs PM decision).
- Long-tail customers with >1B events require separate arch strategy (discuss quota and async erasure contract).
